transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Head of Security, HarborGate), Tom Eldridge (CTO), Rafael Ortega (Legal Counsel)

Summary:
High-level intake on data residency, key management and log redaction needs for HarborGate Capital. Customer leaning toward Hosted initially but with requirement to move to Dedicated or Private deployment if KMS residency/escrow controls not met. Heavy emphasis on GDPR/HIPAA-like controls for payment-related PII, audit trails, and ability to prove key possession/residency for regulators.

Topics covered:
- KMS/HSM integration and key residency (escrow concerns)
- Log retention windows and redaction/pseudonymization options
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for compliance and cost
- Evidence artifacts (SOC2, penetration test reports, audit logs)
- Timeline for pilot and gating criteria for enterprise procurement

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time today. i'm maya from redwood, and derek, our solutions engineer is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: good, thanks. we wanted to use this to, like, lay out the red team and compliance asks. short on time but big picture — need to understand how keys and logs stay within our geofence.
[00:18] Tom: yeah hi, tom here. primary constraint is european residency plus us customer transactions that get routed through our custody layer, so we have a mix of GDPR and financial services regs.
[00:29] Derek: great — and quick note, we can support hosted to start, but there are obviously differences for dedicated and private. we'll walk through keystores, H S M options, and what we can surface in audit artifacts.
[00:40] Rafael: from legal — two quick things: one, do you support key escrow where a third party holds an escrow copy? two, we need to prove chain of custody for decryption keys for auditors.
[00:50] Maya: yes right, so short answer: we integrate with customer-managed K M S; you can bring your keys via K M S provider and we support H S M-backed keys. escrow is a bit nuanced — we don't act as a default escrow holder in hosted mode, but for private deployments we can arrange for HSM in customer VPC and options for dual-control or escrow via a partner.
[01:10] Aisha: okay that nuance matters. so if we do hosted, keys must never leave our K M S region, essentially. is that supported?
[01:18] Derek: in hosted, we do have regional isolation — but with caveats: the control plane remains centralized for multi-region routing. we can do model execution in eu-west-1 hardware and keep k m s calls in-region, but some metadata like request routing logs might go through the control plane depending on plan. if complete control is needed, dedicated or private is safer.
[01:40] Tom: can you expand 'metadata' — what specifically leaves the region in hosted?
[01:46] Maya: we log anonymized usage metrics for billing and tracing. the full request payload can be configured — by default we won't store input payloads in hosted beyond short term for caching, but some customers request stricter retention.
[02:00] Derek: yeah and just to add i'm sorry about earlier typos in docs — the K V cache is separate from persistent logs; the cache is ephemeral. persistent logs and audit trails are where you need to specify retention and redaction.
[02:15] Aisha: redaction is big for us. we need PII redaction at ingestion and then the ability to show auditors that redaction patterns ran correctly. do you have automated redaction or do we need a preprocessing layer?
[02:27] Derek: we offer configurable redaction hooks and you can plug in pre-processing rules during ingestion. there is also a policy-driven redaction service on dedicated/private where you can run regex and ML-based PII detectors before persisting. in hosted it's more templated.
[02:44] Rafael: legal follow-up: retention windows. our compliance group requires tiered retention: 30 days for raw inputs, 365 days for transaction metadata, 7 years for some audit indexes. can redwood adhere?
[02:58] Maya: yes tiered retention is supported in dedicated and private. hosted supports short windows by default but there is an add-on for longer evidence retention — however, evidence extraction for 7 years usually pushes people to private/dedicated due to cost and residency.
[03:12] Tom: and about proof — can you produce signed audit logs? like signed entries that can't be tampered with by sysadmins?
[03:20] Derek: we can produce tamper-evident logs via append-only storage plus signed entries backed by K M S. in private deployments you control the signing keys; in hosted we can support customer-managed K M S to sign logs but there are more operational controls to discuss.
[03:36] Aisha: that last bit is crucial. the auditors insist on customer-controlled signing so they can verify independent of vendor claims.
[03:43] Maya: understood. action on our side: we'll outline exactly how signing works per deployment mode.
[03:48] [04:00] short silence / crosstalk
[04:15] Rafael: on key escrow — is there an option for dual-control where keys require two operators to unlock for emergency decrypt?
[04:23] Derek: yes. H S M providers and K M S policy can enforce multi-party authorization; our private deployment ops runbooks can tie into that. again hosted is limited unless you have customer-managed K M S with those policies enabled.
[04:38] Tom: does redwood support H S M modules you bring to the V P C? or do we have to use cloud provider H S M?
[04:45] Maya: private supports both — you can bring-your-own H S M (BYOHSM) or we can provision an HSM in your V P C using a partner. dedicated may have provider-managed H S M options depending on contract.
[04:58] Aisha: about data residency, we need to ensure logs for EU customers never leave eu geo. can you guarantee that? what about backups and failover?
[05:06] Derek: we can geo-fence primary data plane and backups; in hosted we offer region-locking for data plane and geo-fenced backups as an enterprise option. failover across regions for high availability is possible but that requires contractual agreement around data movement.
[05:24] Rafael: do you have prior customers who've done a similar setup for financial services? any references?
[05:29] Maya: yes, several banks and asset managers have used dedicated or private for similar controls. we'll include redacted reference docs and a short case note in the follow-up.
[05:38] [06:00] Derek: quick technical aside on redaction accuracy — for ML detectors we provide F1 metrics from our evals and you can run your own tests against a prompt set to validate.
[06:12] Tom: latency is a concern. if we go private, can we expect similar latency to hosted? our traders are latency-sensitive on some flows.
[06:20] Derek: private deployed close to your infra will typically reduce RTT; however performance also depends on the instance types and the runtime kernels configured. we can run benchmarks with your latency profiles as a pilot.
[06:34] Aisha: on the procurement front, we need SOC2, ISO 27001, and some pen test summaries. also we need contractual language around right-to-audit and breach notification windows.
[06:45] Maya: not a problem, we'll share SOC2 report and our incident response SLA. breach notification is typically 72 hours for hosted, but can be tightened for enterprise contracts.
[06:55] Rafael: final note from legal — data subject requests: if an EU subject asks for deletion of their data, how is that processed given caching and inferential outputs?
[07:06] Derek: deletion is supported at ingestion level; we also have KV cache invalidation and expunge flows. inferential outputs (like model weights) are not retrained persistently on per-request basis so there isn't an implicit retention in the model. for explainer doc we'll show the deletion flow and proof artifacts.
[07:22] Tom: ok next, timeline: we're aiming for a pilot in january. gating items are K M S residency/escrow answer, retention SLAs, and pricing for dedicated.
[07:32] Maya: perfect, so we'll follow up with a package: K M S integration checklist, privacy/retention config options, reference notes, and a preliminary dedicated pricing estimate.
[07:44] Aisha: please include an explicit note on whether keys must be in our V P C or if cross-account K M S is sufficient for signing.
[07:53] Derek: noted. we will also include a short matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private that maps to compliance controls and what each supports out of the box.
[08:04] Rafael: any blockers on running EU-only pilot? we might want a hardened environment.
[08:09] Maya: none on our side; we will need an agreed scope for the pilot and an infra contact.
[08:18] [08:30] crosstalk / planning next steps

End recap and explicit next steps (read back):
[08:45] Maya: recap — redwood to send K M S and signing explanation, SOC2 + pen test summary, dedicated pricing ballpark, and a matrix of retention and redaction capabilities. harborGate to send regulated data classes and retention policy doc. set pilot week in Jan pending procurement. any additions?
[08:59] Tom: include latency benchmark for private in the pilot plan.
[09:03] Aisha: include the multi-party key control and escrow options clearly.
[09:07] Rafael: legal will review the draft and flag EULA clauses around right-to-audit.

[09:15] Maya: thanks all, we'll get that over.
